subject: Packaging pathways for throughput vs. feature bundles
messages:
From: Nia Harper <niah@averyhealth.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@averyhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging options — projected 500k token spikes and feature needs

Hi Ethan,

Thanks again for the overview last week. We ran the traffic forecast through the infra team and expect regular usage of ~150k tokens/day with occasional spikes up to ~500k in a single hour for short experiments.

Before we lock in a pilot, two quick asks on packaging/pricing:
- If we start on the Compact tier and need to upgrade to a higher-throughput tier mid-quarter, how is proration handled? Is there an immediate new rate or do you do end-of-quarter true-ups?
- We care about per-request feature flags (function calling + streaming) — are those gated into higher tiers or available as add-ons?
- For discounts: if we commit to a 12-month reserved seat/throughput bundle with a 6-month pilot, is there a standard mid-term discount cadence or room to negotiate an initial uplift discount for the pilot?

Attached is a short RFP with our throughput profile and security checklist (Avery_RFP_ThroughputRequirements.pdf). Can you point us to the path that minimizes our risk of throttling while keeping unit economics reasonable?

Also copying Marco (Platform) who will own the technical acceptance criteria.

Appreciate it,
Nia

--
Nia Harper
Head of Platform Partnerships
Avery Health
From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Nia Harper <niah@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@averyhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — projected 500k token spikes and feature needs

Hi Nia — thanks for the detail and the RFP. I reviewed the attachment and sketched three practical paths depending on how conservative you want to be:

1) Elastic-hosted start (lowest friction): Compact tier + on-demand bursting. Bursting is billed at higher per-token than reserved throughput but gives immediate relief during spikes. Upgrades mid-quarter are pro-rated from the time of change; we do not require end-of-quarter true-ups unless you want to convert burst usage into a reserved commit (then we credit back a portion).

2) Reserved throughput (Dedicated-style) for predictable peak windows: reserve a monthly throughput bucket sized for 70–80% of expected max hour throughput and attach a feature bundle (streaming + tool-calls) as part of the seat. Reserved commits give the biggest per-token discount and predictable latency guarantees. Downgrades are allowed on a quarterly boundary with a 30-day notice; early downgrade carries a partial contract adjustment.

3) Hybrid pilot (recommended for Avery): 6-week pilot on Compact with a committed cadence for a dedicated pool if spike patterns justify it. During the pilot we can apply an introductory pilot uplift discount (one-time) and pre-agree the conversion credit if you commit to a 12-month reserved contract afterward.

Feature bundling note: streaming and function/tool calling are available as add-ons on Compact but are bundled into the higher-throughput plan tiers at no extra feature charge. That means you can prototype streaming on Compact (higher per-token) and then move into a reserved tier where those features are included.

I've attached a short overview that maps these paths to expected unit economics given the profile in your RFP (PackagingOptions_Overview.pdf).

Next steps: Ben from Sales will share a couple of pricing scenarios (pilot + 12m convert) with discount ranges and a sample SOW. If that looks good we'd set a technical kickoff and lock a pilot start date.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-minute sync this week if helpful.

Best,
Ethan

--
Ethan Park
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Nia Harper <niah@averyhealth.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — pricing scenarios and pilot discount

Hi Nia — looping in a couple pricing scenarios tied to DEAL-8391 so we have clear options to evaluate quickly. High-level:

Scenario A — Short pilot, then 12m convert
- 6-week pilot on Compact: $0 (waived platform access fee) + bill per-token at pilot rates
- Convert to 12m reserved throughput sized at 75% peak hour: 18% discount on list per-token vs on-demand
- One-time pilot conversion credit equal to 25% of pilot spend applied against month-1 of the reserved commit

Scenario B — Immediate reserved pilot (recommended if uptime/latency SLOs are critical)
- 3-month reserved pilot commit at a small discount (10%) with ability to increase capacity in-place
- Downgrade allowed at quarter boundary; early exits incur a defined shortfall fee (we can cap)

For both scenarios we can include streaming and tool-calls in the reserved tiers (no add-on). We are open to negotiating an extra onboarding credit if you sign within the next 30 days — we typically reserve that for Strategic customers converting within the quarter.

Attached: PricingModel_Scenarios.xlsx (sample numbers + breakpoints).

If you want formal redlines we'll also prepare a Master SOW draft and DocuSign link once you pick a path. I added the HubSpot DEAL-8391 link here for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DEAL-8391

Thoughts on which scenario aligns with your procurement cadence?

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Nia Harper <niah@averyhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options — pricing scenarios and pilot discount

Thanks Ben / Ethan — this is clear and helpful. Marco and I discussed and we want to proceed with Scenario A (6-week pilot, convert to 12m reserved commit if tests meet SLOs). Two remaining asks before we sign:

1) Can you send the Master SOW draft and a DocuSign link so our legal can start parallel review? (we like to reduce legal cycle time)
2) For the conversion credit: please call out the exact timing and mechanism for applying the 25% pilot credit in the SOW (we'd like it applied against the first invoice after conversion).

If you can get both documents in the next 48 hours we'll aim to start the pilot the week of Nov 2.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — excited to get started.

Best,
Nia

--
Nia Harper
Head of Platform Partnerships
Avery Health
